passages.text: After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding back its four winds so that no wind would blow on land or sea or on any tree.
passages.sermon:
John saw a vision after the great day of wrath.
He saw four angels.
The four angels stood at the four corners of the earth.
Each angel held back one of the four winds of the earth.
The angels stopped all wind from blowing on the land.
They stopped all wind from blowing on the sea.
They stopped all wind from blowing on any tree.
passages.original: Μετὰ τοῦτο εἶδον τέσσαρας ἀγγέλους ἑστῶτας ἐπὶ τὰς τέσσαρας γωνίας τῆς γῆς κρατοῦντας τοὺς τέσσαρας ἀνέμους τῆς γῆς ἵνα μὴ πνέῃ ἄνεμος ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς μήτε ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης μήτε ἐπὶ πᾶν δένδρον

passages.text: And I saw another angel ascending from the east, with the seal of the living God. And he called out in a loud voice to the four angels who had been given power to harm the land and the sea: “Do not harm the land or sea or trees until we have sealed the foreheads of the servants of our God.”
passages.sermon:
John saw another angel.
This angel came from the east.
The angel had the seal of the living God.
The angel called out in a loud voice.
He spoke to the four angels.
God had given these four angels power to harm the land and the sea.
The angel said, “Do not harm the land.
Do not harm the sea.
Do not harm the trees.
Wait until we seal the foreheads of the servants of our God.”
passages.original: καὶ εἶδον ἄλλον ἄγγελον ἀναβαίνοντα ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς ἡλίου ἔχοντα σφραγῖδα Θεοῦ ζῶντος καὶ ἔκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ τοῖς τέσσαρσιν ἀγγέλοις οἷς ἐδόθη αὐτοῖς ἀδικῆσαι τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν λέγων Μὴ ἀδικήσητε τὴν γῆν μήτε τὴν θάλασσαν μήτε τὰ δένδρα ἄχρι σφραγίσωμεν τοὺς δούλους τοῦ Θεοῦ ἡμῶν ἐπὶ τῶν μετώπων αὐτῶν

passages.text: And I heard the number of those who were sealed, 144,000 from all the tribes of Israel: From the tribe of Judah 12,000 were sealed, from the tribe of Reuben 12,000, from the tribe of Gad 12,000, from the tribe of Asher 12,000, from the tribe of Naphtali 12,000, from the tribe of Manasseh 12,000, from the tribe of Simeon 12,000, from the tribe of Levi 12,000, from the tribe of Issachar 12,000, from the tribe of Zebulun 12,000, from the tribe of Joseph 12,000, and from the tribe of Benjamin 12,000.
passages.sermon:
John saw a vision from God.
He heard the number of people who were sealed.
God sealed 144,000 people.
These people came from all the tribes of Israel.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Judah.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Reuben.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Gad.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Asher.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Naphtali.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Manasseh.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Simeon.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Levi.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Issachar.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Zebulun.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Joseph.
God sealed 12,000 people from the tribe of Benjamin.
passages.original: Καὶ ἤκουσα τὸν ἀριθμὸν τῶν ἐσφραγισμένων ἑκατὸν τεσσεράκοντα τέσσαρες χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι ἐκ πάσης φυλῆς υἱῶν Ἰσραήλ Ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰούδα δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι ἐκ φυλῆς Ῥουβὴν δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐκ φυλῆς Γὰδ δώδεκα χιλιάδες Ἐκ φυλῆς Ἀσὴρ δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐκ φυλῆς Νεφθαλὶμ δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐκ φυλῆς Μανασσῆ δώδεκα χιλιάδες Ἐκ φυλῆς Συμεὼν δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐκ φυλῆς Λευὶ δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰσσαχὰρ δώδεκα χιλιάδες Ἐκ φυλῆς Ζαβουλὼν δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐκ φυλῆς Ἰωσὴφ δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐκ φυλῆς Βενιαμὶν δώδεκα χιλιάδες ἐσφραγισμένοι

passages.text: After this I looked and saw a multitude too large to count, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue, standing before the throne and before the Lamb. They were wearing white robes and holding palm branches in their hands.
passages.sermon:
John saw a great crowd.
No one could count this crowd.
This crowd came from every nation.
They came from every tribe.
They came from every people.
They came from every language.
They stood before the throne.
They stood before the Lamb.
They wore white robes.
They held palm branches in their hands.
passages.original: Μετὰ ταῦτα εἶδον καὶ ἰδοὺ ὄχλος πολύς ὃν ἀριθμῆσαι αὐτὸν οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο ἐκ παντὸς ἔθνους καὶ φυλῶν καὶ λαῶν καὶ γλωσσῶν ἑστῶτες ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου καὶ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Ἀρνίου περιβεβλημένους στολὰς λευκάς καὶ φοίνικες ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν αὐτῶν

passages.text: And they cried out in a loud voice: “Salvation to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”
passages.sermon:
A great crowd stood before the throne of God and before the Lamb.
They wore white robes.
They held palm branches in their hands.
They cried out with a loud voice.
They said, “Salvation belongs to our God.”
“Our God sits on the throne.”
“Salvation belongs to the Lamb.”
passages.original: καὶ κράζουσιν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ λέγοντες Ἡ σωτηρία τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν τῷ καθημένῳ ἐπὶ τῷ θρόνῳ καὶ τῷ Ἀρνίῳ

passages.text: And all the angels stood around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures. And they fell facedown before the throne and worshiped God, saying, “Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanks and honor and power and strength be to our God forever and ever! Amen.”
passages.sermon:
All the angels stood in a circle around the throne.
The elders stood there too.
The four living creatures also stood there.
The angels fell facedown before the throne.
They worshiped God.
They said, “Amen!
Blessing belongs to our God.
Glory belongs to our God.
Wisdom belongs to our God.
Thanks belongs to our God.
Honor belongs to our God.
Power belongs to our God.
Strength belongs to our God.
This is true forever and ever.
Amen.”
passages.original: Καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι εἱστήκεισαν κύκλῳ τοῦ θρόνου καὶ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν τεσσάρων ζῴων καὶ ἔπεσαν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου ἐπὶ τὰ πρόσωπα αὐτῶν καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ Θεῷ λέγοντες Ἀμήν ἡ εὐλογία καὶ ἡ δόξα καὶ ἡ σοφία καὶ ἡ εὐχαριστία καὶ ἡ τιμὴ καὶ ἡ δύναμις καὶ ἡ ἰσχὺς τῷ Θεῷ ἡμῶν εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων ἀμήν

passages.text: Then one of the elders addressed me: “These in white robes,” he asked, “who are they, and where have they come from?”
passages.sermon:
One of the elders spoke to me.
He asked me a question.
He pointed to the people wearing white robes.
He said, “Who are these people in white robes?”
He also asked, “Where did they come from?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἀπεκρίθη εἷς ἐκ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων λέγων μοι Οὗτοι οἱ περιβεβλημένοι τὰς στολὰς τὰς λευκὰς τίνες εἰσὶν καὶ πόθεν ἦλθον

passages.text: “Sir,” I answered, “you know.” So he replied, “These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
passages.sermon:
One of the elders spoke to me.
He asked about the people in white robes.
I answered him.
I said, “Sir, you know.”
The elder replied to me.
He said, “These people have come out of the great tribulation.”
They washed their robes.
They made their robes white.
They did this by the blood of the Lamb.
passages.original: Καὶ εἴρηκα αὐτῷ Κύριέ μου σὺ οἶδας Καὶ εἶπέν μοι Οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐρχόμενοι ἐκ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς μεγάλης καὶ ἔπλυναν τὰς στολὰς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐλεύκαναν αὐτὰς ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ Ἀρνίου

passages.text: For this reason, they are before the throne of God and serve Him day and night in His temple; and the One seated on the throne will spread His tabernacle over them.
passages.sermon:
These people stand before the throne of God.
They serve God day and night in His temple.
God sits on the throne.
God will cover them with His presence.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτό Εἰσιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ λατρεύουσιν αὐτῷ ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς ἐν τῷ ναῷ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁ καθήμενος ἐπὶ τοῦ θρόνου σκηνώσει ἐπ’ αὐτούς

passages.text: ‘Never again will they hunger, and never will they thirst; nor will the sun beat down upon them, nor any scorching heat.’
passages.sermon:
These people came out of the great tribulation.
They washed their robes.
They made their robes white in the blood of the Lamb.
They stand before the throne of God.
They serve God day and night in His temple.
God protects them.
They will never hunger again.
They will never thirst again.
The sun will not beat down on them.
No scorching heat will harm them.
passages.original: οὐ πεινάσουσιν ἔτι οὐδὲ διψήσουσιν ἔτι οὐδὲ μὴ πέσῃ ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὁ ἥλιος οὐδὲ πᾶν καῦμα

passages.text: For the Lamb in the center of the throne will be their shepherd. ‘He will lead them to springs of living water,’ and ‘God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.’”
passages.sermon:
The Lamb stands in the center of the throne.
The Lamb will be their shepherd.
The Lamb will lead them to springs of living water.
God will wipe away every tear from their eyes.
passages.original: ὅτι τὸ Ἀρνίον τὸ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ θρόνου ποιμανεῖ αὐτούς καὶ ὁδηγήσει αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ ζωῆς πηγὰς ὑδάτων καὶ ἐξαλείψει ὁ Θεὸς πᾶν δάκρυον ἐκ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτῶν
